name: Hezekiah
charge: Trusting in the Lord God of Israel; cleaving to him and keeping his commandments; breaking the brasen serpent; keeping the passover; spreading Sennacherib's letter before the Lord
summary: He opened the doors of the house of the Lord in the first month of his first year, kept a passover Jerusalem had not seen since Solomon, broke the brasen serpent of Moses because Israel burned incense to it, and prayed his way through Sennacherib and through a sentence of death. The one pride of his heart is its own case. This is the rest.
offense: Hezekiah opened and repaired the temple doors in his first year, gathered the priests and Levites, and required them to sanctify themselves and remove the uncleanness left by earlier rulers (2 Chronicles 29:3-11). Reform began with restoring the service that had been neglected, not merely with denouncing the past. He also broke the brazen serpent because Israel burned incense to it (2 Kings 18:4). An object associated with Moses could not be preserved as an idol on account of its history. Faithfulness distinguished the Lord's former use of a thing from the people's present misuse of it. He invited Israel to Passover, provided for priestly service, and arranged faithful distribution of the people's offerings (2 Chronicles 30:1-5; 31:11-21). Prayer accompanied that order: when some ate without the required cleansing, he besought pardon for those who prepared their hearts to seek God, and the Lord heard (2 Chronicles 30:18-20).
judgment: And the Lord was with him; and he prospered whithersoever he went forth. Then Isaiah sent to Hezekiah: that which thou hast prayed to me against Sennacherib king of Assyria I have heard. I will defend this city, to save it, for mine own sake, and for my servant David's sake. Of his sickness: I have heard thy prayer, I have seen thy tears: behold, I will add unto thy days fifteen years; and the shadow went back ten degrees. Thus the Lord saved Hezekiah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and guided them on every side; and he was magnified in the sight of all nations from thenceforth.

He invited Israel to Passover, provided for priestly service, and arranged faithful distribution of the people's offerings (2 Chronicles 30:1-5; 31:11-21). entries.commentary: Hezekiah son of Ahaz begins to reign over Judah in the third year of Hoshea, the last king of Israel before the captivity. He does that which is right according to all that David his father did, removing the high places, breaking the images, and cutting down the groves. He breaks in pieces the brazen serpent Moses made in the wilderness, which had stood from that time and was now being burned incense to, and he calls it Nehushtan.

Hezekiah trusts in the Most High so that none among the kings of Judah, before or after, was like him. He clave to the Most High, kept the commandments, and the Most High was with him so that he prospered. Prospering here does not mean a mansion or luxury, but the blessing that comes from keeping and doing the commandments. He rebels against the king of Assyria and smites the Philistines even unto Gaza. -

In Hezekiah's fourth year Shalmaneser besieges Samaria, and after three years, in Hezekiah's sixth year, Samaria is taken. Israel was not removed all at once but carried away in stages into Assyria. The reason given again is that they obeyed not the voice of the Most High but transgressed His covenant and all Moses commanded. -

Sennacherib king of Assyria comes up against the fenced cities of Judah and takes them. Hezekiah sends to Lakish acknowledging offense and agrees to bear whatever tribute is laid on him. Assyria appoints three hundred talents of silver and thirty talents of gold, so Hezekiah gives all the silver of the house of the Most High and even cuts the gold from the temple doors.

The king of Assyria sends Tartan, Rabsaris, and Rabshakeh with a great host to Jerusalem, and they stand by the conduit of the upper pool. Rabshakeh challenges Hezekiah's confidence, mocking his trust and calling Egypt a bruised reed that pierces the hand of any who lean on it. He argues that because Hezekiah removed the high places, even Judah's own worship is now confined to one altar, twisting the reform into a weakness. He boasts that Assyria came up against the land by the word of the Most High Himself, claiming divine backing to destroy it.

Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah ask Rabshakeh to speak in the Syrian language so the people on the wall will not understand, but he refuses. Rabshakeh cries aloud in the Jews' language, warning the people not to let Hezekiah deceive them or make them trust in the Most High. He promises the people their own vines, fig trees, and waters if they surrender, then a land like their own, seeking to turn them from their king. He asks whether the gods of Hamath, Arpad, Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivah delivered their lands, claiming no god can deliver Jerusalem out of his hand. The people hold their peace and answer not a word, for Hezekiah had commanded silence. Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah come to Hezekiah with their clothes rent and tell him the words of Rabshakeh. --- Topics: [Esau and Edom](/encyclopedia/esau-and-edom) · [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood) · [The Sabbath](/encyclopedia/the-sabbath)

Hezekiah begins to reign at twenty five years old and does that which is right in the sight of the Lord, according to all that David his father had done. In the first month of his first year he opens the doors of the house of the Lord and repairs them, then brings in the priests and Levites and charges them to sanctify themselves and carry the filthiness out of the holy place. He names the sin plainly: the fathers had trespassed, forsaken the Most High, turned their backs on his habitation, shut the doors, put out the lamps, and stopped burning incense and offering burnt offerings. -

Because of this forsaking, the wrath of the Lord was upon Judah and Jerusalem, and he delivered them to trouble, to astonishment, and to hissing, so that their fathers fell by the sword and their sons, daughters, and wives went into captivity. The same warning was spoken over Solomon: turning from the commandments would make Israel a proverb and a byword, an astonishment to all who passed by. That is exactly how the nations look at scattered Israel today. -

Hezekiah purposes in his heart to make a covenant with the Lord God of Israel so his fierce wrath may turn away, and charges the Levites not to be negligent since the Most High chose them to minister and burn incense. The Levites are named and sanctify themselves, cleansing the house of the Lord and carrying every unclean thing out to the brook Kidron over sixteen days. They report to the king that they have cleansed all the house of the Lord, the altar of burnt offering, the showbread table, and even the vessels that king Ahaz had cast away in his transgression.

Hezekiah rises early, gathers the rulers, and brings seven bullocks, seven rams, seven lambs, and seven he goats for a sin offering for the kingdom, the sanctuary, and Judah. The priests kill the animals and sprinkle the blood on the altar, making reconciliation with the blood to make an atonement for all Israel. Under the law, atonement required animal sacrifice, but the reconciliation the Most High provides now is through the death of his son. You cannot be reconciled to someone you were never joined to, so the reconciliation is for the house of Israel his people. -

Hezekiah sets the Levites in the house of the Lord with cymbals, psalteries, and harps according to the commandment of David, Gad the seer, and Nathan the prophet. When the burnt offering begins, the song of the Lord begins with trumpets and instruments, and all the congregation worships until the offering is finished. The king and princes command the Levites to sing praise with the words of David and Asaph the seer, and they sing with gladness and bow their heads in worship. -

Once the people are consecrated they bring so many sacrifices and thank offerings that the sanctified priests are too few to flay all the burnt offerings, so the rest of the Levites help until the work is ended. The Levites were more upright in heart to sanctify themselves than the priests, and the burnt offerings, fat, and drink offerings are in abundance. The service of the house of the Lord is set in order, and Hezekiah and the people rejoice that the thing was done suddenly, done decently and in order. -

Now that the temple is cleansed and the priests sanctified, Hezekiah sends letters to all Israel and Judah, even to Ephraim and Manasseh, calling them to keep the Passover at Jerusalem. The king and congregation agree to keep it in the second month, because the priests had not sanctified themselves sufficiently and the people had not yet gathered in the first month. They make a proclamation from Beersheba to Dan to come keep the Passover, for they had not done it for a long time in the way it was written. -

The posts carry the letters through all Israel and Judah with the king's charge: turn again unto the Lord God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, and he will return to the remnant escaped from the kings of Assyria. Do not be like your fathers who trespassed and were given up to desolation, and do not be stiffnecked, but yield to the Lord and enter his sanctuary so his fierce wrath may turn away. If they turn again, their captive brethren and children will find compassion and return to the land, for the Lord is gracious and merciful and will not turn his face away from those who return to him.

The posts pass from city to city through Ephraim and Manasseh to Zebulun, but the people laugh them to scorn and mock them, the same mockery Israel meets today when the truth is preached. Nevertheless some of Asher, Manasseh, and Zebulun humble themselves and come to Jerusalem, and in Judah the hand of God gives them one heart to do the commandment of the king. The great congregation removes the altars and incense altars in Jerusalem and casts them into the brook Kidron. -

They kill the Passover on the fourteenth day of the second month, and the priests and Levites, ashamed, sanctify themselves and bring the burnt offerings into the house of the Lord. Because many in the congregation were not sanctified, the Levites take charge of killing the Passover for everyone not clean. Many of Ephraim, Manasseh, Issachar, and Zebulun eat the Passover otherwise than it was written, but Hezekiah prays that the good Lord pardon everyone who prepares his heart to seek God, and the Lord hearkens and heals the people. Grace and mercy are present here in the Old Testament.

The children of Israel keep the feast of unleavened bread seven days with great gladness, then take counsel and keep another seven days, fourteen days in all, all in one mind and one heart. Hezekiah and the princes give thousands of bullocks and sheep, and all the congregation, the priests, the Levites, and the strangers out of Israel rejoice together. There is great joy in Jerusalem, for since the days of Solomon there had not been the like, and the priests and Levites bless the people and their prayer reaches heaven, his holy dwelling place. -

When the feast is finished, all Israel present goes out to the cities and breaks the images, cuts down the groves, and throws down the high places and altars throughout Judah, Benjamin, Ephraim, and Manasseh. Then every man returns to his own possession and city, the reformation now reaching beyond the temple into the whole land. This obeyed the law directly: rather than intermarry with the nations, Israel was to destroy their altars and burn their graven images. -

Hezekiah appoints the priests and Levites to their courses for burnt offerings, peace offerings, and thanksgiving, and sets the king's portion for the daily, Sabbath, new moon, and feast offerings as written in the law. He commands the people in Jerusalem to give the portion of the priests and Levites so they may be encouraged in the law, and the people bring in abundance the firstfruits of corn, wine, oil, honey, and the tithe of all things. They lay the tithe in heaps from the third to the seventh month, and when Hezekiah and the princes see the heaps they bless the Lord and his people Israel. -

Hezekiah questions the priests about the heaps, and Azariah the chief priest of the house of Zadok answers that since the people began bringing offerings they have had enough to eat with plenty left, for the Lord has blessed his people. Hezekiah commands chambers prepared in the house of the Lord, and appoints faithful Levites over the offerings, tithes, and dedicated things to distribute the oblations to their brethren by courses, to great and small alike. The portions are given by genealogy to the priests and Levites and to their little ones, wives, sons, and daughters, for they sanctified themselves in holiness.

Hezekiah does throughout all Judah that which is good and right and true before the Lord his God. In every work he begins in the service of the house of God, in the law, and in the commandments to seek his God, he does it with all his heart and prospers. This is the charge on every one of us: do the work with everything you have as unto the Lord, and keep his laws, or it will not be blessed. You cannot halfway walk in the truth and expect to grow. -

When Hezekiah hears the reproach of Assyria he rends his clothes, covers himself with sackcloth, and goes into the house of the Most High, then sends his servants to Isaiah the prophet. He calls it a day of trouble, rebuke, and blasphemy, and asks Isaiah to lift up prayer for the remnant that is left. This follows chapter 18, where Rabshakeh the messenger of Sennacherib told Judah their God was no different from the gods of the nations Assyria had already destroyed. Isaiah, Micah, and Hosea prophesied in this same period, so much of what is read in one is found in the others. Isaiah returns the word of the Most High: fear not the blasphemy, for the Most High will send a blast upon Sennacherib, and he shall hear a rumor, return to his own land, and fall by the sword there.

Rabshakeh returns and finds the king of Assyria warring against Libnah, having departed from Lachish. Hearing that Tirhakah king of Ethiopia has come out to fight against him, Sennacherib sends messengers again to Hezekiah with a threatening letter. The letter mocks Judah's trust, listing the nations and kings Assyria destroyed, saying their gods could not deliver them, so Jerusalem will not be delivered either.

Hezekiah receives the letter, reads it, goes up to the house of the Most High, and spreads it before Him. He prays acknowledging the Most High as God alone of all the kingdoms of the earth, maker of heaven and earth, and asks Him to bow down His ear and hear the words that reproached the living God. He confesses that the gods Assyria cast into the fire were no gods but the work of men's hands, wood and stone, and asks the Most High to save them so all the nations may know He alone is the Lord God. The prayer of Hezekiah is that the Most High show His power and prove His people are the chosen and that He is the one true living God. This is a righteous prayer, the same praying for the downfall of enemies and for righteous judgment to come upon them.

Isaiah sends word that the Most High has heard the prayer against Sennacherib, and the virgin daughter of Zion despises and laughs him to scorn. The Most High asks whom Sennacherib has reproached and blasphemed, for he has lifted up his eyes on high against the Holy One of Israel. Israel is laughing at the enemy, for it is already written that they lose. Assyria boasted with the multitude of his chariots to cut down cedars and dry up rivers, the same as a nation today boasting of its army, military, and political system. The Most High answers that He did it and formed it of ancient times; He gave Assyria the very ability to lay fenced cities waste as ruinous heaps for His own purpose. Because their rage and tumult came up to His ears, the Most High will put His hook in Sennacherib's nose and His bridle in his lips, and turn him back the way he came, which joins with the blast promised in verse 7. -

The sign given to Hezekiah is that they shall eat what grows of itself two years, and in the third year sow, reap, and plant vineyards. The remnant of the house of Judah shall again take root downward and bear fruit upward, for out of Jerusalem and Mount Zion a remnant shall escape. This is twofold: a remnant came out of Assyria and into Babylon, and it also speaks of the remnant today, for the zeal of the Lord of hosts will perform it.

The Most High declares the king of Assyria shall not come into this city, nor shoot an arrow there, nor come before it with shield, nor cast a bank against it. By the way that he came, by the same shall he return, and he shall not enter the city. The Most High will defend the city to save it for His own sake and for His servant David's sake; what He did to Samaria He will not do to Jerusalem.

That night the angel of the Most High goes out and smites the camp of the Assyrians, killing a hundred fourscore and five thousand, all dead corpses by morning. A score is twenty, so this is a hundred and eighty-five thousand slain. Israel did not lift a finger; the Most High handled the battle for them, for it is not by might but by His spirit. This is praying for the death of the enemy and for righteous judgment. Sennacherib departs and dwells at Nineveh, and as he worships in the house of Nisroch his god, his sons Adrammelech and Sharezer smite him with the sword and flee, and Esarhaddon his son reigns in his stead, fulfilling the word of verse 7. -

Hezekiah falls sick unto death, and Isaiah brings the word to set his house in order, for he shall die and not live. Hezekiah turns his face to the wall and prays, asking the Most High to remember how he walked before Him in truth and with a perfect heart, and he weeps sore. Before Isaiah leaves the middle court the word returns: the Most High has heard his prayer and seen his tears, will heal him, add fifteen years, and defend the city for His own sake and for David's sake. Isaiah applies a lump of figs to the boil and Hezekiah recovers, showing that remedies and herbs go together with prayer, for healing is in the hand of the Most High. -

Hezekiah asks for a sign that the Most High will heal him and that he shall go up to the house of the Most High on the third day. Isaiah offers the shadow going forward ten degrees or back ten degrees, and Hezekiah answers that going forward is a light thing, but let it return backward ten degrees. Isaiah cries to the Most High and He brings the shadow ten degrees backward on the dial of Ahaz, reversing the natural course of the sun as proof of His power.

Berodach-baladan son of Baladan king of Babylon sends letters and a present to Hezekiah, having heard he had been sick; this is the introduction of Babylon, still only a province under Assyria at this time. Hezekiah hearkens to them and shows them all his precious things, his silver, gold, spices, ointment, and armor, holding nothing back, trusting his enemies because of the gift. Isaiah asks what the men saw and where they came from, then declares that all in the house shall be carried into Babylon, and Hezekiah's own sons shall be eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon. Hezekiah answers that the word of the Most High is good, content that peace and truth be in his days. This same account is given in [Isaiah 39](/bible/isaiah/39). -

The rest of the acts of Hezekiah, including how he made a pool and a conduit and brought water into the city, are written in the chronicles of the kings of Judah. Bringing water into the city is vision and planning like no other; this is nation building. Hezekiah sleeps with his fathers, and Manasseh his son reigns in his stead.

After these acts of faithfulness Sennacherib king of Assyria enters Judah and encamps against the fenced cities, thinking to win them for himself. Hezekiah takes counsel to stop the waters of the fountains outside the city, repairs the broken wall, raises towers, builds another wall, and makes darts and shields in abundance. Our people are resourceful and skilled, doing the work themselves. He sets captains over the people and comforts them: be strong and courageous, for there be more with us than with him; with him is an arm of flesh, but with us is the Lord our God to help us and fight our battles. -

Sennacherib sends servants to Jerusalem asking on what the people trust that they abide in the siege, and claims Hezekiah is persuading them to die by famine and thirst. He mocks that Hezekiah took away the high places and altars and commanded worship at one altar, twisting obedience to the commandment into a weakness. He argues that no god of any nation delivered its people from his hand, so neither will the God of Hezekiah. This is the same seed the world plants to make Israel weary and turn a people off one accord. -

Sennacherib's servants speak yet more against the Lord God and against his servant Hezekiah, and he writes letters to rail on the Lord God of Israel. They cry with a loud voice in the Jews' speech to the people on the wall to frighten and trouble them so they might take the city. They speak against the God of Jerusalem as against the gods of the peoples of the earth, which were only the work of men's hands. The one true God is the God of Israel, not an idol like the false gods of the nations.

Hezekiah the king and Isaiah the prophet, the son of Amos, pray and cry to heaven over this railing. The Lord sends an angel that cuts off all the mighty men of valour, leaders, and captains in the camp of Assyria, so Sennacherib returns with shame to his own land, and his own sons slay him with the sword in the house of his god. Thus the Lord saves Hezekiah and Jerusalem and guides them on every side, and many bring gifts to the Lord and presents to Hezekiah, so he is magnified in the sight of all nations, a picture of the gifts the nations will bring back to Israel in the kingdom.

In those days Hezekiah is sick to death, prays to the Lord, and is given a sign. But Hezekiah renders not according to the benefit done to him, for his heart is lifted up in pride, and wrath comes upon him and upon Judah and Jerusalem. When things go well, do not get puffed up and make it about yourself. Then Hezekiah humbles himself for the pride of his heart, he and the people of Jerusalem, so that the wrath of the Lord does not come upon them in his days. -

Hezekiah has exceeding riches and honour, making treasuries for silver, gold, precious stones, and spices, and storehouses for corn, wine, oil, and cattle, for God gives him very much substance. He stops the upper watercourse of Gihon and brings it straight down to the west side of the city of David, and prospers in all his works, the plumbing he built for Jerusalem. When the ambassadors of Babylon come to inquire of the wonder, God leaves him to try him and know his heart. Hezekiah then sleeps with his fathers, is buried in honour among the sons of David, and Manasseh his son reigns in his stead. --- Topics: [Clean and Unclean Meats](/encyclopedia/clean-and-unclean-meats) · [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood) · [The Sabbath](/encyclopedia/the-sabbath)

verses.text: Now it came to pass in the third year of Hoshea son of Elah king of Israel, that Hezekiah the son of Ahaz king of Judah began to reign.
Twenty and five years old was he when he began to reign; and he reigned twenty and nine years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name also was Abi, the daughter of Zachariah.
And he did that which was right in the sight of the Lord, according to all that David his father did.

He removed the high places, and brake the images, and cut down the groves, and brake in pieces the brasen serpent that Moses had made: for unto those days the children of Israel did burn incense to it: and he called it Nehushtan.
He trusted in the Lord God of Israel; so that after him was none like him among all the kings of Judah, nor any that were before him.
For he clave to the Lord, and departed not from following him, but kept his commandments, which the Lord commanded Moses.
And the Lord was with him; and he prospered whithersoever he went forth: and he rebelled against the king of Assyria, and served him not.
Hezekiah began to reign when he was five and twenty years old, and he reigned nine and twenty years in Jerusalem. And his mother’s name was Abijah, the daughter of Zechariah.
And he did that which was right in the sight of the Lord, according to all that David his father had done.
He in the first year of his reign, in the first month, opened the doors of the house of the Lord, and repaired them.
And he brought in the priests and the Levites, and gathered them together into the east street,
And said unto them, Hear me, ye Levites, sanctify now yourselves, and sanctify the house of the Lord God of your fathers, and carry forth the filthiness out of the holy place.

For our fathers have trespassed, and done that which was evil in the eyes of the Lord our God, and have forsaken him, and have turned away their faces from the habitation of the Lord, and turned their backs.
Also they have shut up the doors of the porch, and put out the lamps, and have not burned incense nor offered burnt offerings in the holy place unto the God of Israel.
Wherefore the wrath of the Lord was upon Judah and Jerusalem, and he hath delivered them to trouble, to astonishment, and to hissing, as ye see with your eyes.
For, lo, our fathers have fallen by the sword, and our sons and our daughters and our wives are in captivity for this.
Now it is in mine heart to make a covenant with the Lord God of Israel, that his fierce wrath may turn away from us.
My sons, be not now negligent: for the Lord hath chosen you to stand before him, to serve him, and that ye should minister unto him, and burn incense.

And Hezekiah sent to all Israel and Judah, and wrote letters also to Ephraim and Manasseh, that they should come to the house of the Lord at Jerusalem, to keep the passover unto the Lord God of Israel.
For the king had taken counsel, and his princes, and all the congregation in Jerusalem, to keep the passover in the second month.
For they could not keep it at that time, because the priests had not sanctified themselves sufficiently, neither had the people gathered themselves together to Jerusalem.
And the thing pleased the king and all the congregation.

So they established a decree to make proclamation throughout all Israel, from Beer–sheba even to Dan, that they should come to keep the passover unto the Lord God of Israel at Jerusalem: for they had not done it of a long time in such sort as it was written.

For a multitude of the people, even many of Ephraim, and Manasseh, Issachar, and Zebulun, had not cleansed themselves, yet did they eat the passover otherwise than it was written. But Hezekiah prayed for them, saying, The good Lord pardon every one
That prepareth his heart to seek God, the Lord God of his fathers, though he be not cleansed according to the purification of the sanctuary.
And the Lord hearkened to Hezekiah, and healed the people.

And the children of Israel that were present at Jerusalem kept the feast of unleavened bread seven days with great gladness: and the Levites and the priests praised the Lord day by day, singing with loud instruments unto the Lord.

And Hezekiah spake comfortably unto all the Levites that taught the good knowledge of the Lord: and they did eat throughout the feast seven days, offering peace offerings, and making confession to the Lord God of their fathers.
And the whole assembly took counsel to keep other seven days: and they kept other seven days with gladness.

For Hezekiah king of Judah did give to the congregation a thousand bullocks and seven thousand sheep; and the princes gave to the congregation a thousand bullocks and ten thousand sheep: and a great number of priests sanctified themselves.

And all the congregation of Judah, with the priests and the Levites, and all the congregation that came out of Israel, and the strangers that came out of the land of Israel, and that dwelt in Judah, rejoiced.
So there was great joy in Jerusalem: for since the time of Solomon the son of David king of Israel there was not the like in Jerusalem.
Then the priests the Levites arose and blessed the people: and their voice was heard, and their prayer came up to his holy dwelling place, even unto heaven.
And thus did Hezekiah throughout all Judah, and wrought that which was good and right and truth before the Lord his God.
And in every work that he began in the service of the house of God, and in the law, and in the commandments, to seek his God, he did it with all his heart, and prospered.
And Hezekiah received the letter of the hand of the messengers, and read it: and Hezekiah went up into the house of the Lord, and spread it before the Lord.

And Hezekiah prayed before the Lord, and said, O Lord God of Israel, which dwellest between the cherubims, thou art the God, even thou alone, of all the kingdoms of the earth; thou hast made heaven and earth.

text.text: Now it came to pass in the third year of Hoshea son of Elah king of Israel, that Hezekiah the son of Ahaz king of Judah began to reign.
Twenty and five years old was he when he began to reign; and he reigned twenty and nine years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name also was Abi, the daughter of Zachariah.
And he did that which was right in the sight of the Lord, according to all that David his father did.

He removed the high places, and brake the images, and cut down the groves, and brake in pieces the brasen serpent that Moses had made: for unto those days the children of Israel did burn incense to it: and he called it Nehushtan.
He trusted in the Lord God of Israel; so that after him was none like him among all the kings of Judah, nor any that were before him.
For he clave to the Lord, and departed not from following him, but kept his commandments, which the Lord commanded Moses.
And the Lord was with him; and he prospered whithersoever he went forth: and he rebelled against the king of Assyria, and served him not.
Hezekiah began to reign when he was five and twenty years old, and he reigned nine and twenty years in Jerusalem. And his mother’s name was Abijah, the daughter of Zechariah.
And he did that which was right in the sight of the Lord, according to all that David his father had done.
He in the first year of his reign, in the first month, opened the doors of the house of the Lord, and repaired them.
And he brought in the priests and the Levites, and gathered them together into the east street,
And said unto them, Hear me, ye Levites, sanctify now yourselves, and sanctify the house of the Lord God of your fathers, and carry forth the filthiness out of the holy place.

For our fathers have trespassed, and done that which was evil in the eyes of the Lord our God, and have forsaken him, and have turned away their faces from the habitation of the Lord, and turned their backs.
Also they have shut up the doors of the porch, and put out the lamps, and have not burned incense nor offered burnt offerings in the holy place unto the God of Israel.
Wherefore the wrath of the Lord was upon Judah and Jerusalem, and he hath delivered them to trouble, to astonishment, and to hissing, as ye see with your eyes.
For, lo, our fathers have fallen by the sword, and our sons and our daughters and our wives are in captivity for this.
Now it is in mine heart to make a covenant with the Lord God of Israel, that his fierce wrath may turn away from us.
My sons, be not now negligent: for the Lord hath chosen you to stand before him, to serve him, and that ye should minister unto him, and burn incense.

And Hezekiah sent to all Israel and Judah, and wrote letters also to Ephraim and Manasseh, that they should come to the house of the Lord at Jerusalem, to keep the passover unto the Lord God of Israel.
For the king had taken counsel, and his princes, and all the congregation in Jerusalem, to keep the passover in the second month.
For they could not keep it at that time, because the priests had not sanctified themselves sufficiently, neither had the people gathered themselves together to Jerusalem.
And the thing pleased the king and all the congregation.

So they established a decree to make proclamation throughout all Israel, from Beer–sheba even to Dan, that they should come to keep the passover unto the Lord God of Israel at Jerusalem: for they had not done it of a long time in such sort as it was written.

For a multitude of the people, even many of Ephraim, and Manasseh, Issachar, and Zebulun, had not cleansed themselves, yet did they eat the passover otherwise than it was written. But Hezekiah prayed for them, saying, The good Lord pardon every one
That prepareth his heart to seek God, the Lord God of his fathers, though he be not cleansed according to the purification of the sanctuary.
And the Lord hearkened to Hezekiah, and healed the people.

And the children of Israel that were present at Jerusalem kept the feast of unleavened bread seven days with great gladness: and the Levites and the priests praised the Lord day by day, singing with loud instruments unto the Lord.

And Hezekiah spake comfortably unto all the Levites that taught the good knowledge of the Lord: and they did eat throughout the feast seven days, offering peace offerings, and making confession to the Lord God of their fathers.
And the whole assembly took counsel to keep other seven days: and they kept other seven days with gladness.

For Hezekiah king of Judah did give to the congregation a thousand bullocks and seven thousand sheep; and the princes gave to the congregation a thousand bullocks and ten thousand sheep: and a great number of priests sanctified themselves.

And all the congregation of Judah, with the priests and the Levites, and all the congregation that came out of Israel, and the strangers that came out of the land of Israel, and that dwelt in Judah, rejoiced.
So there was great joy in Jerusalem: for since the time of Solomon the son of David king of Israel there was not the like in Jerusalem.
Then the priests the Levites arose and blessed the people: and their voice was heard, and their prayer came up to his holy dwelling place, even unto heaven.
And thus did Hezekiah throughout all Judah, and wrought that which was good and right and truth before the Lord his God.
And in every work that he began in the service of the house of God, and in the law, and in the commandments, to seek his God, he did it with all his heart, and prospered.
